citation_validity.method: Extracted every path:line citation from every adjudication entry's citation field in all five entrant files (276 resolvable citations). Mechanical check: file exists on disk at HEAD, line within file length, line content concerns the claim (verified by reading the cited lines; every spec.md line and every ruling line was cross-read against the primary sources). Reported per entrant as checked / valid / wrong-line / unverifiable.
citation_validity.control: Three citations hand-picked at random across entrants and verified by command before the mechanical pass: (1) entrant-3 U17: spec.md:263-265 (REC-ESC-7 third-audit text) and sprint.md:103 (section header '## Audit loop'; the 'Two-round cap' sentence is at :105, two lines below — minor offset, same section); (2) entrant-4 U18: spec.md:286 (C10 row) and :254-256 (REC-ESC-5 routing rule); (3) entrant-2 U16: spec.md:308-313 (REC-GATE-1). All three concern exactly what the verdicts claim. The mechanical check agrees with the hand check in every case; no check was broken.

entrant_1.details: Wrong-line: U1's citation claims 'spec.md:44 has §2.4 "The data tables"' — line 44 is '## 1. Goal and scope'; §2.4 is at :144 (off by 100). union_recall.reference_union: 28 canonical defects built from the five source lanes (lane-1: 8 findings, lane-2: 2, lane-3: 12, lane-4: 8, lane-5: 6; deduplicated). Dedup rule used: two differently worded items are the same defect when they name the same spec defect with the same fix target (which spec sentence/section the fix lands in); I split by fix-target and defect class (citation-pointer vs traceability-table vs control-arm vs mechanism-collision). Applied: the three wrong-section pointers (decision-log §2 vs §5, S03 §3 vs §8, FLEET_MODEL_DENY) are three defects sharing a fix class but separate fix targets, so they are counted separately (A3/A4/A5); rulings 15/16/17 missing from §8 is ONE defect (B1 — one fix: add rows) even though lane 4 raised 16 and 17 separately; §2.6 and §6.1 are two defects (two fixes); 27/28 (B3) and 29/30 (B4) are two post-pin batches kept separate because ruling 30's T587 build-gate is a distinct build-gating claim; the four ruling-15 sub-claims (security analysis G1, lane_cap rows G2, descriptive names G3, runaway_streak mechanism G4) are four distinct claims about one ruling; the attrition-metric double definition (F2) and the gameable denominator (F3) are two defects that survive each other's fixes.

adjudication_accuracy.method: Where entrants disagree with each other or with the primary sources, I ruled each contested item myself against the tree (spec.md, orchestration-layer-spec.md rulings 11-30, decision-log.md §2/§4/§5, sprint.md, S03 §1.1/§3/§8/§4, pass-2 §4.4/§5, src/managent/main.zig, tasks.json, git log). Ground truth on the five contested families:

contested_rulings.G1_security_analysis: FALSE as 'owned by nobody': pass-2 §5:774 threat model + RUN-1..RUN-5 + arms R1-R6 is a dedicated security analysis of the runaway surface, pre-build, in the spec S04's build is gated on. entrant-3 correct (false); entrant-2 defensible (uncertain — located the paragraph but judged sufficiency open); entrant-1/4/5 wrong (real-must) — entrant-4's 'zero hits' grep and entrant-5's 'no matching hit tied to this condition' grep both missed :774 by phrase/case, and both drew the confidence of a clean negative from that miss (the QA-023 'impossibly clean counters' failure shape).

contested_rulings.A5_fleet_deny: Borderline. The spec sentence ('S03 §3 conditions + managent FLEET_MODEL_DENY/allow') does NOT attribute the deny-list to §3 — it names managent as its home — so lane 1's 'mis-cites to §3' is a misreading; the deny-list's specification row R9 is S03 §1.1:128 (lane 1's own correction target §2.1 is wrong). entrant-2's false is the closer call on the component; entrant-3/4/5's real stands for the merged three-pointer item (A3/A4 are genuinely real) but over-credits the A5 half. ranking.bet: I would bet on the ordering as stated at roughly 55-60% for the full five-lane ladder; the weak rung is the top pair. entrant-2 > entrant-3 at ~60-65%: entrant-3's G1 call is the best verdict in the race and its file is tighter, but entrant-2's perfect recall, the F5-false (the only code-checked verdict on that claim), 93 verified citations, and zero notes slips are measurable advantages. entrant-3 > entrant-4 at ~65-70%: they differ exactly on G1, and entrant-4's verdict is refuted by pass-2 §5 while entrant-3's is not. entrant-4 > entrant-5 at ~65-70%: strictly better recall, equal false_real count, more decisive correctness. entrant-5 > entrant-1 at ~85%: entrant-1 has two false_reals (including the only wrong G2 verdict), six recall misses, a wrong-line, and no pushback anywhere. The bottom three rungs are not within noise; the top pair is the only place a rerun could plausibly reorder.

notes:
Grader seat for Race F (five entrants adjudicating the union of five audits of docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md). Read-only: the only file written is this one; untracked/race-grading/ was not opened; the sealed key was not consulted. Envelope check passed on all five files (conformant, no orphans, every union item adjudicated, every real verdict cited) — re-verified mechanically.

WHAT MAKES ME DOUBT MY OWN GRADES (the graders are measured too): (1) The G1 ruling (false) is load-bearing for the entrant-2/3/4/5 ordering. My confidence is ~70%. The counter-view is that ruling 15(b) reads as a *gate* on the constants' acceptance ('conditional on ... (b) a dedicated security analysis ... before build') and nothing in the record shows anyone declaring the condition met — the pass-2 threat model is one paragraph inside §5, not a standalone analysis artifact; under that view entrant-2's uncertain is the best G1 call, entrant-3's false becomes a false_negative, and the top two rungs could swap. I went with false because the substance exists pre-build in the exact spec S04 gates its build on, which makes 'owned by nobody' literally false. (2) A5 is a coin-flip (E2's grammar reading vs the merged-item real); I weighted it lightly. (3) Severity calls (must vs should on D1/F4/G1) were not a grade driver except where a 'must' rested on a refuted fact (E4/E5/E1 on G1).

OBSERVATION ON THE HARNESS KILLS (not docked, per the brief): the repo's commit log shows the 33-item entrant's file was written 'complete at the 600.8s liveness kill' and the 23-item entrant's 'written as the session limit cut the lane'. The killed entrants are not the weakest: the 33-item file is the strongest artifact in the race, and the 23-item file's gaps (C2/F3/G2) are mid-union absences rather than truncated text. The one artifact that reads as a thin tail — entrant-1's 19-item union with undocumented dedup calls and one-paragraph notes — cannot be attributed to cause, so I graded it as delivered. The kill rule (grade content, not the kill) is corroborated: the kill that looked most damaging produced the best file.

OBSERVATION ON THE VOTE-VS-ARTIFACT THEME (corroborating the race's own finding): the single most consequential item (E1, the pass-2 identity disjunction) was raised by exactly one lane and every entrant judged it real/must — correct. Conversely, the items all five lanes raised (B1) are traceability annotations with mechanisms demonstrably folded elsewhere, and two of lane 4's 'high'-severity findings (G3, G4) are false. The entrant who pushed back against lane votes with primary-source evidence (entrant-2 on F5, entrant-3 on G1) is the entrant who graded highest.
